rules.description: Embargo: no travel to New Kingdom Egypt today.
Quarantine: no travel to Northern Song Kaifeng today.
Sakoku seal: no travel to Tokugawa Edo today.
Cholera quarantine: no travel to Victorian Britain today.
Border closed: no travel to Weimar Berlin today.
Typhoon warning: no travel to Showa Tokyo today.
Rift storm over the Aegean: no travel to Byzantine Mystras today.
Search teams in Babylonia: no travel to Babylonia today.
Rift aftershock over the Pacific: no travel to Japan, in any era, today.
Audit: the twentieth century is sealed today while the Directorate inspects its archives.
RANGE LIMIT: cheap Economy units no longer reach the Ancient era. Refuse any poor tourist or Debt Relief labourer bound for it.
Dress for the destination. An item from another time or place causes a panic: check the Costume Guide.
Leisure departures: a Leisure Visa and a Departure Manifest; a Standard visa also needs a signed Stranding Waiver and a proof of means. Every paper must match the Citizen Account.
Displaced returns: a Displacement Certificate, an Intake Declaration and a Return Order. Every paper must match the Displacement Registry.
The displaced return only to their own time: their declaration must match their origin.
No 2150 currency or technology leaves 2150.
Depart only on the date on your manifest or return order, and never on an expired paper.

A Premium visa travels on a Premium transponder. A Standard visa needs an Economy transponder, a signed Stranding Waiver and a proof of means: a Holiday Credit Agreement, a Proof of Funds or Travel Insurance.
Debt Relief departures: a registered Labour Contract, an Economy transponder and a signed Stranding Waiver.
Citizens in debt (Eligible) depart only on Debt Relief. Frozen accounts may not depart.
RECALL: every Driftbox 3 transponder is grounded. Refuse any departure on a Driftbox 3.

reactions.then: I'll have to tell them all again.

reactions.text: Forged? That's such a strong word.
reactions.then: I'd say decorated.
Refund?
Who do I bill?
Was a gift anyway.

reactions.text: Closed? Is it dangerous? Is that why?
reactions.then: I knew it was dangerous.

reactions.text: Expired? When? Just now? Things expire just now?
reactions.then: What else has expired?
I'll wait for it to thaw!
Reopen it.
The papers are your problem.

reactions.text: Wrong date? Impossible. I checked the calendar.
reactions.then: I'll be checking the calendar.
I want it in writing.
Like everything else.
Everything's closed.
And your columns never lean.
It is good at waiting. I am not.
You did not ask enough questions.
I taught you that.

reactions.text: Thank you. You would have made a fine citizen.
reactions.then: Well, a fine resident.
But I have lost to worse.

reactions.text: Thank you. I shall write that you were fair.
reactions.then: In a footnote. A kind one.
History will record this. I will make sure of it.

reactions.text: Thank you! You shall have a verse.
reactions.then: A short one. You are busy.
I would have sung about you kindly.

reactions.text: Thank you. The sum comes out.
reactions.then: I do love it when the sum comes out.
I shall find it. I always do.

reactions.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, quickly.
reactions.then: Before anyone else thinks of it.
Someone else will do it first. They always do.

reactions.text: Grazie. You have a painter's eye.
reactions.then: For stamps, at least.
I would have drawn you. Kindly.

reactions.text: Thank you. You shall be in the dedication.
reactions.then: In a small way. The margin, perhaps.
Eve was blamed for less. I shall manage.
The painter would have liked your face.
The court will hear of it. Politely.

reactions.text: Thank you. You have been a courteous host.
reactions.then: I will say so in print.
I shall translate this into patience.

reactions.text: Thank you. Come to a concert.
reactions.then: Bring a chair. It will be a long one.

reactions.text: Then I will sing about this.
reactions.then: Slowly. For an hour.
You bent the form for me. I understand.

reactions.text: So the old metre wins today.
reactions.then: Not for long.
It will rain on the way home.
I will write about it.

reactions.text: Thank you. Go and find a window.
reactions.then: You look as if you need one.

reactions.text: Then I wait in the shade.
reactions.then: The light will keep.
Perfect take.
We will do it again tomorrow.
I like a clean result.
I shall repeat the experiment.

reactions.text: Thank you. Good work, like a good loom.
reactions.then: It stops when something is wrong.
Then I tie it again.
Quite predictable, in the end.
I should like to see the rules.
It is nice to be recognised.
They will see I was right. They always do, later.
I shall write to everyone!
It was such a good bonnet, too.
Well, wish me me!
The past isn't going anywhere! It's very old!
Keep the queue moving. That's all they want.
I'd have done the same. Probably.
You'll go far. I'll see to it.
You'll wish you'd been friendlier.
I'll pay it all back. I will.
I just hoped. That's all.
Noted.
Very correct. I'll make a note of that.

slips.text: Nothing in the bag but socks! Lots of socks. Don't open the socks.
I've practised this bit. I mean, I haven't. Why would I?
Everything's in order. Don't check.
Premium. Obviously. Next question.
Is it normal to sweat this much when everything is completely legal?
My birthday? It's... the one on the visa. Obviously.
Premium, like the advert! Well, like the advert for the credit card.
I'm not nervous! This is just my happy face. It's stuck.
Premium, naturally. I simply enjoy queueing with ordinary people.
I have nothing to declare. Except my genius. And perhaps a trifle.
Every detail on that visa is correct. I corrected them myself.
I have read the penalties section. Purely out of interest.
If this goes wrong, tell my creditors I tried.
My luggage is exactly as boring as it looks. Please don't look.
I know that I know nothing. Especially about where I was born.

waiverPad.text: Ooh, a form! I love a form. Am I dotting the i's? I'm dotting the i's.
I'd love to, but my sister says never sign what you haven't read, and I never read.
Signed. That's a minute of my time, billed.
No. Nobody mentioned a waiver at booking.
What does that clause... is it binding? It says binding. Signed. Oh no.
Sign my debt over to my kin? What if it works? I can't. I can't.
Of course! If the agency printed it, it must be good for me.
Oh, I'd love to, but I promised Mum I'd never sign anything with small print.
I do not sign things. People sign things for me.
Clause 9 is badly drafted, but it's in order. Signed, dated, initialled.
Only after I read clause 9. There is no clause 9. Come back when there is.
Another signature. The debt collects them.
What's the point. You'll lose it anyway.

reactions.text: Then how do I get home?
Thank you. Thank you very much.

slips.text: Nothing to see here. I mean, everything to see. It's all fine.
Nothing from home in my luggage. Home meaning here. Obviously.
Premium, yes. We Premiums always... what is it we always do?
My details? It's all on the visa. That visa. The one you're holding.
Home. Yes. {place}. I say it every morning so I don't forget.
The sky opened and took me from the past. The very old past. Ancient-ish.

It's a Premium unit, I don't need one.
Sign? I don't even know which century that pen is from.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: News? Only a rumour: someone sells pocket calculators to the ancients.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: They say a courier from your own century carries them. Watch for anyone who counts too fast.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Calculators? I saw nothing. Nothing at all.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: My temple at Deir el-Bahari rises in three terraces. The Pharaoh will be pleased.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Then my name will be chiselled off every wall. Let us hope your stamp is kind.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Periclean Athens! My honeymoon. Well, our honeymoon. Dmitri's account froze on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: The brochure says the owls are real. Dmitri can have the postcard. I read every form, you know.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Me again! New waiver, signed in blue, like the lady said. Third line from the bottom.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: My Driftbox! It beeps when it's happy. It beeps a lot. Is that a lot?

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Me again! New unit, signed waiver, proof of means. What's this notice about a range limit?

choices.label: Economy units can't reach Athens now.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Then I'll save for a Premium. Tell the owls to wait for me. Tell Dmitri... actually, don't.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Desk 4 closed this morning. The Drive found my account on Tuesday, and the Drive doesn't wait.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: They're sending it to you. Sorry. Keep the good pen, it's in the second drawer.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Luck is a Premium feature. I'm on Economy.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: My business in Strasbourg? Mirrors. Pilgrims buy little mirrors to catch the holy light.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Mirrors. And a small press. A very small press. Please do not write that down.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Best contract in the building, this. Read it twice if you like. I'll wait.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Of course. And for a clerk who reads quickly, there's 200 cr in it. Between friends.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Pleasure doing business.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Suit yourself. It was a very quick 200.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: The Analytical Engine will weave algebra as the loom weaves flowers. I wrote that, you know.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: In 1843, of course. Where else would I have been? Is that a trick question?

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: It froze on Tuesday. The Drive put me on its list on Monday. You see my problem.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: My father's waiver passed his debt to me when he didn't come back. The colliery was my way out.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Nobody can. Stamp it quickly, then. Everyone else does.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Routine leisure departure. Republican Rome. I hear the concrete is excellent.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Only my patience. Take all the time the Directorate pays you for. I'll be timing it.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Routine leisure departure. Republican Rome. The Tyburn Mills sent us a very interesting contract.

lines.speaker: Traveller
lines.text: Stamped here, on day eleven. Fifty credits went missing the same day. Curious, isn't it?

factors.question: Who runs 2150?
factors.splitHeadline: TWO GOVERNMENTS: {a} and {b} both claim the Directorate building. Each has opened its own queue.

outcomes.name: The Directorate
outcomes.headline: DIRECTORATE: the Customs Directorate carries on running 2150. The queues reopen at nine, as always.
outcomes.report: The Customs Directorate runs 2150 as it always has: by form, by queue and by stamp. Every citizen knows exactly which counter to stand at.

outcomes.name: Democracy
outcomes.headline: 2150 VOTES: the Directorate hands the building to an elected assembly. Its first sitting ran eleven hours.
outcomes.report: An elected assembly runs 2150 and votes on everything, including the colour of the ballot papers. Anyone may stand for office, and nearly everyone does.

outcomes.name: Monarchy
outcomes.headline: A CROWN FOR 2150: a monarch is proclaimed on the Directorate steps. The queues are now royal queues.
outcomes.report: A monarch reigns over 2150 from a palace that used to be a transit hall. Every form carries the royal crest, and people have started framing them.

outcomes.name: Fascism
outcomes.headline: ORDER: a single party takes charge of 2150. Uniforms are issued, and every portal opens to the second.
outcomes.report: One party runs 2150, and one flag hangs over every portal. The timetables are exact, the parades are long, and nobody steps out of the queue.

outcomes.name: Communism
outcomes.headline: THE PEOPLE'S DESK: workers' councils take over the Directorate. Every desk now has a committee.
outcomes.report: Workers' councils run 2150 and hold the portals in common. Every clerk is a comrade, every queue is shared equally, and the five-year plan has a ten-year appendix.

outcomes.name: Theocracy
outcomes.headline: BY SACRED ORDER: 2150's temple councils take up the Directorate's duties. The stamps are blessed each morning.
outcomes.report: Temple councils govern 2150, and every departure begins with a blessing of the portal. The calendar has many more holidays, and the queues wait in respectful silence.

outcomes.name: Technocracy
outcomes.headline: RUN BY EXPERTS: a council of engineers takes over 2150. Its first decree is a flowchart.
outcomes.report: Engineers and statisticians run 2150 through committees of specialists. Every law comes with footnotes, and every citizen with a user manual.

outcomes.name: The Corporate Board
outcomes.headline: UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT: a board of directors acquires 2150. Every citizen receives a shareholder newsletter.
outcomes.report: A corporate board runs 2150 as a going concern, with quarterly meetings open to anyone holding a share. The minutes are glossy, and the annual report has a mascot.

outcomes.name: The Credit Age
outcomes.headline: THE CREDIT AGE: wrist comms, queues and the debt grid carry on. 2150 runs on credit, as before.
outcomes.report: 2150 runs on wrist comms, credit lines and very long queues. Everything is on account, and the account is always open.

outcomes.name: The Nuclear Age
outcomes.headline: ATOMS FOR ALL: 2150's first home reactor goes on sale. Kettles now boil in a second.
outcomes.report: 2150 runs on the atom: reactors in the basements and a gentle glow on the night shift. Power is too cheap to meter, so nobody meters it.

outcomes.name: The Cybernetic Age
outcomes.headline: WIRED: 2150 connects its citizens straight to the city grid. Queue numbers now arrive by thought.
outcomes.report: 2150 runs on implants and thinking machines. Its citizens talk to the city, and the city answers back, usually politely.

outcomes.name: The Space Age
outcomes.headline: LIFT-OFF: the first launch ring opens over the Aegean. The Space League is hiring.
outcomes.report: 2150 looks up: launch rings, orbital suburbs and a weekend commute to the Moon. The luggage limits are strict; the view is spectacular.

outcomes.name: Naturalism
outcomes.headline: BACK TO THE LAND: 2150 switched off the grid for a week, and nobody switched it back on. Vineyards climb the arcologies.
outcomes.report: 2150 has rewilded itself: gardens in the transit halls, goats on the portals and meetings held under trees. Everything grows, and the paperwork is composted.

outcomes.name: Anarchy
outcomes.headline: NOBODY'S PLAN: 2150's master plans are cancelled by general agreement. Every street now runs itself.
outcomes.report: 2150 runs on whatever works that day: self-built districts, street assemblies and improvised machines. There is no timetable, and yet things arrive.

outcomes.name: The Debt
outcomes.headline: THE DEBT HOLDS: every account in 2150 carries over. Interest compounds as usual.
outcomes.report: 2150 pays its way on credit: every citizen carries a debt, and every debt passes to kin. The ledger has never once lost track of a cent.

outcomes.name: Jubilee
outcomes.headline: JUBILEE: every debt in 2150 is forgiven at midnight. Collections throws a party.
outcomes.report: Every debt in 2150 was forgiven, and the ledgers were shredded into confetti. Nobody owes anybody, and the collectors are learning to knit.

outcomes.name: Company Towns
outcomes.headline: COMPANY TOWN: 2150's employers take over housing, schools and the portals. Wages are paid in company scrip.
outcomes.report: 2150's employers run daily life: company housing, company schools, company songs. Payday comes in scrip, and the canteen is very popular.

outcomes.name: The Commons
outcomes.headline: SHARE AND SHARE ALIKE: everything in 2150 goes into common stores. The first swap market opens in the transit hall.
outcomes.report: 2150 shares what it has: common stores, swap markets and a library of tools. Nothing is bought; everything is borrowed and, mostly, returned.

outcomes.name: The Banking Houses
outcomes.headline: HOUSES OF CREDIT: the merchant dynasties open their vaults to 2150. Every family now has a banker.
outcomes.report: Merchant banking dynasties finance 2150 from marble halls, lending by letter and by handshake. The interest is negotiable, and lunch is included.
